en: One Scroll of the Ritual Manual for the Recitation of Bhaisajyaguru Tathāgata,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daixingshan Monastery, by Imperial Decree.
At one time, the Buddha was dwelling beneath the Vīṇā-vimukta tree together with thirty-six thousand bhikṣus and twelve divine kings.
Together with his retinue— the eight classes of divine beings, including devas and nāgas,
and the great sovereign deities— having spoken this Dharma within such a great assembly, he [concluded].
The great assembly heard this and all were filled with joy.
This is what is called the "Concluding Vow Divine Mantra.
Then the Bhagavān spoke the mantra, saying:
Namo bhagavate vīrasena-vaiḍūrya-parivārāya tathāgatāya | Tadyathā | Oṃ vīrashe vīrasa samudgate svāhā | If there be anyone who receives and upholds this mantra...
It can uproot all grave sins from past births and deaths within one’s own body;
one shall no longer undergo the three miserable realms,
escape the nine untimely deaths, and transcend all suffering.
For the root seal and mantra:
with the left and right hands, interlace the eight fingers from the index fingers downward into the palms.
Moving the two thumbs back and forth, recite the mantra:
*Oṃ jñānakīri svāhā*. Next, perform the protection and praise:

*Sarvabuddhānāṃ sarvasattvānugārūṇatvamakāra-dharmatām adhitiṣṭha mām kuru vai narye āvara-tathāgatamahānayārthasiddhyai namaḥ siddhārtha.* *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja, in One Scroll.*
